title: docs (cluster, connectors): lane 2 now also converges connector definitions on every replica (#28002); cluster.mdx §6.2 and the connectors reload row still say otherwise
body:
domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia

Filing gate: ① docs that will contradict the runtime at named locations. Found by the #28002 card thread (PR #28028) and filed by the `domain:server` seat, because both pages are outside that card's file surface. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Drift (lands with PR #28028)

PR #28028 (#28002) makes the automation plugin's metadata-mutation listener queue the connector reconcile for a `connector` mutation that is not a draft. Through lane 2 (`metadata.mutated`), a connector definition saved active, published or deleted on one replica now converges every replica. A direct active save (`PUT /api/v1/meta/connector/:name`) now re-materialises the writing replica too. No new cluster channel is added.

1. `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`, §6.2. The lanes table (:336) gives lane 2's converging state as "ObjectQL's OBJECT registry", and the "Lane 2 — `metadata.mutated`" subsection (:418 onward) describes only that. Both gain the connector instances that the automation plugin re-materialises from the same replay.
2. `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx:458`, the failure-modes row "A bad entry arrives via runtime reload (Studio publish / dev reload)". It should name the paths that now reach the reconcile: a publish, a direct active save, or a delete, on any replica.

## Wanted

State the lane 2 connector convergence in the words §6.2 already uses: one signal and no second channel, with the peer re-reading the shared store. Update the reload row's trigger list.

⛔ Do not edit before PR #28028 merges. Until then the texts are still true. `connectors.mdx` is also edited by #28016's PR (a new failure-modes row), so check for that and merge `main` first.

## Dedupe

#28002 / PR #28028 (runtime), #27977 / PR #28010 (the measurement), #28016 (the same table, a different row). No open card covers these lines.
